title: Come at the Morning Hour
description: Come at the Morning Hour in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 463, “Seasons for Prayer”, where the book credits them to Briggs' Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come at the morn-ing hour, Come, let us kneel and pray; Prayer is the Chris-tian pil-grim's staff To walk with God all day.

lines: Come, let us kneel and pray;
Prayer is the Christian pilgrim's staff
To walk with God all day.
Sweet is that shelter from the sun
In the weary heat of day.
And finding there the house of God,
With heaven then close the day.
O, it is sweet to say,
I sleep, but my heart waketh, Lord,
With Thee to watch and pray.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
